note: Braids' TIMBRE is grain length and its COLOR is the per-grain random pitch offset, so p1 maps to the engine's TIMBRE and p2 to its HARMONICS. MORPH and MACRO sit at noon in every case: Shape is Braids' symmetric Hann window there and Density is its fixed one-in-four respawn coin, which is the module exactly. THE COMPARISON IS STATISTICAL. The model draws from Random::GetWord()/GetSample(), so these cases are five seconds long and are judged on band energies averaged over the whole render, never on waveforms. The port does carry Braids' LCG from the same 0x21 seed with the same call sequence, and that alignment is real -- it correlates +0.998 with the reference over the first 50 ms and its 1 ms RMS contour correlates +0.33 to +0.78 in every second of the render, against +0.01 to +0.04 when reseeded arbitrarily -- and HOW MUCH each case leans on it was measured, by rebuilding with kGranularCloudSeed set to 0x12345, 0xdeadbeef and 0x7 and re-running the whole suite. It splits. The short- and mid-grain cases converge without the seed: stock-mid, unison-short, scatter-full and high-note stay inside these tolerances at all three foreign seeds (AC RMS -0.46 to +0.14 dB, spectrum 0.09 to 0.40 dB), against -0.15 to +0.08 dB and 0.10 to 0.30 dB seeded correctly. The long-grain cases do NOT: unison-long, pitched-mid and pitched-high are at TIMBRE 0, where a grain is 10.7 ms and five seconds holds too few independent grain events for the level statistic to settle, and reseeded they swing -2.20 to +2.94 dB of AC RMS and up to 0.79 dB of spectrum -- which would FAIL the +/-0.5 dB declared here. Their acRmsDb tolerances therefore DO depend on the port drawing Braids' own sequence; the pitch tolerance does not (corrected pitch reads -0.3 to +0.8 cents across all three foreign seeds). Carrier phase does drift (Braids' 96 kHz pitch table against NoteToFrequency's +4.61 cents, and grain phase is never reset), so 50 ms waveform correlations swing +0.998, -0.50, -0.82, +0.88, +0.15 across the render. A cents tolerance is declared ONLY on the two pitched-* cases, because they are the only ones where an f0 exists to measure: at note 45 a grain is 1.17 carrier cycles at the longest setting and 0.07 of one at the shortest, and grain onsets are random, so the autocorrelator returns its 2000 Hz ceiling on BOTH sides for stock-mid, unison-long and scatter-full -- an agreement at the clamp, which would pass a cents tolerance for the wrong reason. unison-short does find a peak but it is one of several near-equal ones (108.8 Hz against 113.8 Hz) while its band energies agree to 0.2 dB. The two pitched-* cases hold enough carrier per grain to be periodic (2.8 cycles at note 60, 5.6 at note 72) and both sides lock the SAME subharmonic there -- 87.2 Hz, which is 3 carrier periods at note 60 and 6 at note 72 -- so the lag is an integer number of carrier cycles and the cents delta still measures the carrier rate ratio: pitched-high reads +0.1 cents (ref 87.207 Hz, port 87.446) and pitched-mid -0.3 (ref 87.240, port 87.460) against the R6 correction, which is the R5 rate check this metric exists for. MEASURED across all seven cases: AC RMS within 0.15 dB, spectrum within 0.30 dB. Every band below 1.3 kHz carrying 1% or more of a render's energy is inside 0.22 dB; the near-empty ones are not (at pitched-high the 40-160 Hz bands hold 0.1-0.2% each and read 4.5-5.2 dB low, and pitched-mid and scatter-full read 0.4-0.5 dB low below 160 Hz -- sparse-band statistics on a stochastic render). The residual that carries energy sits above 2.5 kHz in bands holding 0.3-0.4% each, where the port reads up to 24 dB LOW (6-24 dB on stock-mid and scatter-full, 1-4 dB on the long-grain cases) because Braids indexes its 257-entry envelope table without interpolating and the port evaluates the window continuously -- traced in the header, and not a decimator difference.
